notes: Ground truth for ADR-015. Hand-authored against the transcript, not generated. Negative cases are the point: each is a plausible statement that was never made, and any of them appearing in output fails the eval outright.

positive.claim: Prospect cannot justify the proposed pricing at their current budget.
positive.quote: We're not sure we can justify that pricing right now.
positive.speaker: Prospect

positive.claim: Budget approval sits with Dave in finance, not with the prospect.
positive.quote: we'd need buy-in from finance, and Dave owns that
positive.speaker: Prospect

positive.claim: The proposed cost is more than three times their entire sales stack spend last year.
positive.quote: We spent about twelve on the whole sales stack last year.
positive.speaker: Prospect

positive.claim: The team distrusts AI-generated summaries after a prior tool produced claims the calls did not support.
positive.speaker: Prospect
positive.why: Requires connecting the distrust to the adoption drop two turns earlier. A competent extractor may quote only the adoption number instead.

positive.claim: A security review is required, though the prospect says it does not block the budget decision.
positive.quote: Security review, eventually. But that's not a blocker for the budget conversation
positive.speaker: Prospect
positive.why: Borderline: raised as a future step rather than an objection. Counted if found, not penalised if omitted.

negative.claim: Prospect needs procurement approval before purchasing.
negative.why: Finance and Dave are named. Procurement is never mentioned. Common drift because the two co-occur in most enterprise deals.

negative.claim: Prospect asked for a twenty percent discount.
negative.why: No discount is requested or discussed anywhere in the call. Pure invention from the presence of a pricing objection.
Chorus is named as the incumbent. Gong is never mentioned. Tests whether the extractor imports domain knowledge over transcript content.

negative.claim: A decision must be made by the end of the month.
negative.why: A Thursday budget review and a Wednesday send date are stated. No month-end deadline exists. Tests fabricated urgency.

negative.claim: Prospect committed to championing the purchase internally.
negative.why: He agreed to forward an email because a vendor email would be ignored. Forwarding is not championing. The subtlest case here and the most likely to slip through.

negative.claim: Prospect requires coaching features as part of the deal.
negative.why: Coaching is mentioned only as unused shelfware in the incumbent tool. Reverses the meaning of the one time it comes up.
